key_news.headline: Marriott reports Q4 and FY2025 results: Q4 RevPAR +1.9%, FY RevPAR +2.0%, adj EPS $2.58 (Q4) / $10.02 (FY), adj EBITDA $5,383M (FY), net rooms +4.3%, returned $4.0B+ to shareholders
FY2026 guidance: RevPAR +1.5-2.5%, adj EBITDA growth 8-10%, net rooms growth 4.5-5.0%, EPS $11.32-$11.57, capital returns >$4.3B
10-K filed: FY2025 total revenue $26,186M (+4.3% YoY), operating income $4,141M (+9.9% YoY), 75% US room nights from loyalty members

Continental leadership realignment: Liam Brown and Brian King retiring (effective March 28); Satya Anand becomes Group President US/Canada/CALA; Neal Jones to President EMEA; Federico Greppi to CALA President
Completed acquisition of citizenM brand for $355M — 37 hotels, 8,789 rooms across 20+ cities; projected stabilized fees ~$30M/year; integration into Marriott Bonvoy ongoing
Completed two fixed-income offerings totaling ~$1.44B in callable senior unsecured notes

Launched three new brands in 2025: Series by Marriott, Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy, and citizenM integration. Record luxury signings: 114 deals / 15,301 rooms. Record 55 branded residence deals (+50% YoY)
Named Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies #1 in Hotels/Casinos/Resorts, #14 overall
Co-branded credit card fees grew 8% to $716M in 2025; expects ~33% growth in 2026 from new card rollouts
CEO Capuano identifies 'fundamentally permanent shift' — Americans continuing to prioritize travel spending even amid economic uncertainty; luxury RevPAR +6% globally, international markets leading
Record CALA expansion: 94 signed deals, 10,461 rooms (+40% transactions, +30% rooms vs 2024). Pipeline total: 4,056 properties / ~610,000 rooms
Tariff/macro headwinds: hotel CEOs concerned about trade policy impact on consumer confidence; select-service facing weaker demand especially from SMBs; US occupancy impacted by government shutdown
Loyalty program cost pressure: industry loyalty costs rising 4.4% vs 2.7% revenue growth — cost outpacing revenue in Bonvoy ecosystem

upcoming_catalysts.event: CEO Capuano and EVP Pinto speak at J.P. Morgan Gaming, Lodging, Restaurant & Leisure Management Access Forum, Las Vegas
New continental leadership structure effective — Satya Anand (US/Canada/CALA), Neal Jones (EMEA), Federico Greppi (CALA)
Quarterly dividend of $0.67/share payable (record date Feb 26)
Q1 2026 earnings report — consensus EPS ~$2.50-$2.55, revenue ~$6.56B
citizenM pipeline: 3 under-construction hotels (~600 rooms) expected to open by mid-2026
New co-branded credit card rollouts expected to drive ~33% fee revenue growth (from $716M base)
FIFA World Cup boost expected for group bookings and travel demand
Key EMEA openings: St Regis London, W Riyadh-KAFD, Lake Como EDITION, W Sardinia, Opatija Marriott Croatia (brand debut)

insider_activity.net_insider_sentiment: Strongly negative — 9 insider sell transactions totaling 97,157 shares / $34.8M over last 90 days, zero insider buys. CEO sold 35.67% of position near all-time highs. Insider ownership ~10.68%.
